s1.syndrome_frame: Acute right lower quadrant abdominal pain with fever and elevated inflammatory markers
salient_findings: Abdominal CT scan showing a swollen and thickened tubular structure with a pericecal collection
key_facts: 24-hour history of right iliac fossa pain
History of laparoscopic appendectomy 8 months earlier
Pain in the right lower quadrant without peritoneal signs
Abdominal CT scan showing a swollen and thickened tubular structure
Pericecal collection adjacent to surgical clips

raw.syndrome_frame: Acute right lower quadrant abdominal pain with fever and elevated inflammatory markers
salient_findings: Abdominal CT scan showing a swollen and thickened tubular structure with a pericecal collection

shortlist.label: Appendiceal stump appendicitis
shortlist.why_kept: History of laparoscopic appendectomy and current presentation of right iliac fossa pain with fever and elevated inflammatory markers

shortlist.label: Pericecal abscess
shortlist.why_kept: Abdominal CT scan showing a pericecal collection adjacent to surgical clips

shortlist.label: Cecal diverticulitis
shortlist.why_kept: Abdominal CT scan showing a swollen and thickened tubular structure at the cecal pole

shortlist.label: Typhlitis
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated white-blood-cell count and C-reactive protein level, consistent with an infectious or inflammatory process

shortlist.label: Meckel's diverticulitis
shortlist.why_kept: Right lower quadrant pain and elevated inflammatory markers, with a possible connection to the patient's surgical history

raw.rationale: The patient's history of laparoscopic appendectomy and the presence of a swollen and thickened tubular structure at the cecal pole with a pericecal collection adjacent to surgical clips on the CT scan support this diagnosis, given the timeframe and symptoms presented.

rejected.label: Pericecal abscess
rejected.why: While there is a pericecal collection, the primary issue appears to be with the appendiceal stump itself, making this less likely as the primary diagnosis.

rejected.label: Cecal diverticulitis
rejected.why: There's no specific indication of diverticula in the provided information, making this less likely.

rejected.label: Typhlitis
rejected.why: Typically associated with neutropenia, which is not indicated in this patient with a high white-blood-cell count.

rejected.label: Meckel's diverticulitis
rejected.why: The location and description of the swollen structure, along with the history of appendectomy, do not support Meckel's diverticulitis as the most likely diagnosis.
